note: Curated descriptive names for the decompiled flat DOS/4G image (stage 07). Addresses are image-relative (flat image imported at base 0). These are OUR analysis conclusions: each entry is added as its meaning is established from reading decompiled.c, and the docs/ notes carry the evidence. g_mode_flag gates init in main and toggles behavior across many subsystems; exact semantics TBD. The RNG names (rng_*) and asteroid-gen names (asteroid_*) are documented in docs/mechanics/rng.md and docs/mechanics/asteroid-creation.md. The game itself names these objects asteroids (the universe's colonizable worlds, each with its own surface); earlier drafts called them galaxies, which the game never does. asteroid_create makes a new asteroid node (rolls size class, surface width and seed); asteroid_place finds a free sector-grid slot and sets the node position (mode 0x3e8 = edge-frame free-slot search starting from a random edge cell, used for in-game top-ups, mode 0x3e9 = random cell + bounded random walk, used by the new-game fill, param<1000 = explicit cell index); asteroid_set_pos writes the +0x54/+0x58 position; asteroid_set_surface rolls the surface style bytes +0x51/+0x52 from the 0xa460/0xa488 tables. asteroid_place_near_oldest places a new asteroid a random 40-110 units from an existing asteroid of the same type (the per-type lists live at 0xd218, counts at 0xd238, flags at 0xd239, stride 0x210, indexed by the asteroid's +0xd0 type byte), re-rolling until it is >32 units (distance^2 > 0x400) from every other asteroid. This budding is called ONLY from the new-game field setup (3 call sites: 0xfd9f, 0xfdcd, 0xfe20); it does NOT run during play, where the count is kept up by the main-loop gate (asteroid_create + asteroid_place 0x3e8 at the map's outer frame). asteroid_prune_overlaps (0x137d4, one call site from the new-game fill) destroys still-untyped (+0xd0==0) asteroids within 90 units of a typed one. asteroid_setup_type_cells (0x152e4) writes each type's initial cell offsets +0xd214/+0xd216 and the 0x10 flag periodically. obj_list_move_front (0x21314) unlinks a node and reinserts it at the list head (used by obj_list_pop and on placement give-up). asteroid_set_type assigns the +0xd0 type byte and bumps the per-type count; asteroid_destroy unlinks an asteroid and decrements the per-type and global (0xca20) counts. The map is a sector grid: [0xcdb0]/[0xcdb4] hold the cell dimensions loaded from the 0x16d90 table by [0x16d64] (map-size index), and [0xcdb8]/[0xcdbc] hold the width/height in units (cells * 0x20). [0x16d64] and [0x16d65] (map size / density) select the density-ceiling byte at 0xa398 (offset 3*size+density), read against the live count 0xca20 every 8 ticks to decide when to spawn a new asteroid; the same ceiling is read from the per-scenario 6-byte config table at 0xa33c indexed by the scenario index 0x16fd0. [0x16d68] is the per-race presence bitmask (bits 9..14), [0x16d70] the number of type-table rows. asteroid_gen_start_values rolls the 10 per-planet starting values into +0x6c; asteroid_setup_start_values copies them from a same-type asteroid, a static table, or an RNG perturbation; asteroid_rank_start_values scores the ten values against the per-slot divisor table and stores the best index at +0x53; obj_list_pop removes and returns the head node of an intrusive list. The 0x5bfa4 occupancy grid is a 32x32 byte grid of occupied sector cells rebuilt from the object list on each placement. The locals section renames function-scoped register/stack names (iVar3, sVar1, in_EAX, ...); entries are added only where the meaning is confirmed by disassembly and documented in docs/.
